Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.state

Class EyeState

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.state.EyeState
public final class EyeState extends Object
Per-mob, mutable, mid-life eye state — the override layer that sits on top of the shared datapack config (EyeConfigModel).

State lives in the mod-owned persistent entity compound and survives entity save/load, dimension changes, aging, mob conversion, and a player leaving the End (copy(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity, net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity)). The loader-specific persistence bridge maps that compound onto each platform's entity storage. Three pieces:

  • somegoogly:hasGooglyEyes — the on/off flag, rolled at spawn and mutable mid-life (shears remove, slimy eye adds).
  • somegoogly:eyeVariantRoll — the 0..1 roll that selects the mob's placement variant, assigned at first join and redrawn by a slimy-eye application.
  • somegoogly:eyeOverrides — an optional compound of per-mob appearance overrides (iris/cornea tint, glow), applied to all of the mob's eyes.

The read helpers and EyeState.Snapshot are side-safe. Server mutation methods write a complete coherent transition and then broadcast one snapshot to the entity's trackers (and the entity itself when it is a player); sendTo(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer) brings one new tracker up to date. Packet handling installs a snapshot without sending it back to the server.

  • Method Details

    • copy

      public static void copy(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity source, net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity target)
      Carry the whole eye state from an entity Minecraft is replacing to its replacement (a mob conversion, or a player leaving the End), so the replacement keeps its eyes instead of rolling fresh. Copying before or after the replacement joins its level both work: an initialized target is never re-rolled, and the broadcast reaches whoever already tracks it.

    • getVariantRoll

      public static float getVariantRoll(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity entity)
      The mob's stored placement-variant roll (0..1), assigned at first join and redrawn when a slimy-eye application turns eyes on. Maps onto the current age config's weighted variants. Defaults to 0 (the first variant) when unset. A stored value outside 0..1 (an edited save) reads clamped into range, and a non-finite one as 0.

    • hasEyes

    • isDefaultState

      public static boolean isDefaultState(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity entity)
      Whether this entity's state matches what a freshly created client entity already assumes: no eyes and no appearance overrides. The start-tracking and spawn-time syncs skip the packet in this case; a mid-life mutation always sends, because the client may then hold a snapshot that has to be transitioned back to the default.

    • isInitialized

      public static boolean isInitialized(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity entity)
      Whether the server has made this entity's one-time natural-eye decision.

    • initialize

      public static void initialize(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity entity, boolean hasEyes, float variantRoll)
      Store the one-time natural-eye decision and placement roll. Broadcasts only when the decision turned eyes on: an eyeless outcome already equals every client's implicit default, so the eyeless spawn — the overwhelming majority — costs no packet. The eyed broadcast is kept so a player who is already tracking when this runs is corrected; later trackers get it from the start-tracking sync.

    • readProperties

      public static AppearanceOverride readProperties(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity entity)
      Read the mob's appearance override as AppearanceOverride (AppearanceOverride.EMPTY when none). The override compound is serialized via the shared AppearanceOverride codec — the same schema an eye item carries — so item↔mob transfer is a straight property copy.
